Issue Number: close #52001 

Problem Summary:
conflict.strategy cannot be used with tikv-importer.parallel-import and tikv-importer.backend = "local" and conflict.precheck-conflict-before-import = true
### What changed and how does it work?
allow parallel import with conflict detection

issue_context.title: conflict.strategy cannot be used with tikv-importer.parallel-import and tikv-importer.backend = "local" and conflict.precheck-conflict-before-import = true
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

parallel import data with two lightning
config is : [conflict]\nprecheck-conflict-before-import = true\nstrategy=\"replace\"\n[tikv-importer]\nparallel-import = true

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
import successfully
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
fail with 
```
2024-03-21T21:22:11.310+0800    INFO    host/host.go:52 Execute command error   {"command": "/tidb-lightning \"-c\" \"/tmp/tidb-lightning.toml\"", "exit code": 1, "stdout": "Verbose debug logs will be written to /tmp/lightning.log.2024-03-21T13.22.11Z\n\n", "stderr": "tidb lightning encountered error: [Lightning:Config:ErrInvalidConfig]conflict.strategy cannot be used with tikv-importer.parallel-import and tikv-importer.backend = \"local\" and conflict.precheck-conflict-before-import = true\n", "error": "command terminated with exit code 1"}
```
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

master

review_comments: Now， we will not distinguish whether it is a logical import, right?

I removed the check of 
```
if c.Strategy != NoneOnDup {
		if i.ParallelImport && i.Backend == BackendLocal && c.PrecheckConflictBeforeImport {
```
Since now we can support parallel import with preprocess conflict detection for local backend.

Originally this was not supported because preprocess and post-import conflict detection are not allowed to be used together, so only conducting preprocess conflict detection may still result in conflicts in the scenarios of parallel import.
So now we support preprocess + post-import conflict， post-import conflict。 the post-import conflict will always enabled, right?
yes. If we set `conflict.strategy` (except `none`), the post-import conflict will always enabled.
